precepts.text: Keep my commandments and live, and my law as the apple of thine eye. If you want to have life, you must keep God's laws; there are no two ways about it.
precepts.point: The first came out red, all over like an hairy garment: it was important for that to be mentioned, because everybody was of the same complexion before. Notice they did not mention the brother's color; when Esau came out red, they had to document it.

note.label: I Come In Peace

precepts.why:
Proverbs 7:2 finishes what Genesis 2:7 opened. God “breathed into his nostrils the breath of life; and man became a living soul,” and that breath of life is his statutes and commandments. Solomon says it plainly: “Keep my commandments, and live; and my law as the apple of thine eye.”

If you want to have life, you must keep God’s laws; there are no two ways about it. The man who is not keeping the Lord’s statutes and commandments is dead, no matter what the Christian pastor tells him about not having to keep them.

This matters for the story of Jacob and Esau. The two came from the same belly, but “two manner of people shall be separated from thy bowels.” One people keeps the law of their God and lives; the other lives another way, like Esau who cried “Feed me, I pray thee, with that same red pottage.” We are not supposed to be eating blood; our food has to be cooked. But you know how they did the Negroes: they wanted to be just like their masters, so they started eating all the garbage Esau eats. The way back to life is to keep his commandments and hold his law as the apple of our eye.

precepts.text: A woman with the attire of an harlot, and subtil of heart. The physical again, meant to entice, and it works. Solomon knew how intoxicating it is; he said not one woman in a thousand.
precepts.point: Y'all take chess and spades seriously, seeing moves ahead and counting books, but not marriage. She looks good, I have to marry her so I can have her.

note.label: Marriage Beyond Romance: From Eden to Modern Confusion

precepts.why:
“And, behold, there met him a woman with the attire of an harlot, and subtil of heart.” There is the physical again: the attire of an harlot and subtil of heart. She is trying to entice, and you fall for it. It works.

Here Solomon warns about being captured by appearance. How does he know these things? He said not one out of a thousand of the women he dealt with. He knew, and he probably knew before the thousandth. It goes to show how intoxicating it can be. You get caught up.

That is the thread through David on the roof in 2 Samuel 11:2. Shechem saw Dinah and took her: violence and massacre. Samson, she pleased him well: betrayal and blindness. David saw Bathsheba's beauty and had to have her: adultery and murder. Absalom, celebrated for his own beauty: pride and rebellion. And the strange women, being beautiful, lead to ruin.

That is why the Bible rarely makes much of the beauty of wives. Rebecca is known for her character, her hospitality and her faith; Zipporah's beauty is never described; Elizabeth is called righteous, not beautiful. What is highlighted in our foremothers is righteousness, obedience, wisdom and faith. The Bible doesn't deny attraction; it just isn't the foundation.

precepts.text: Keep my commandments, and live; and my law as the apple of thine eye.
precepts.point: Keep my commandments and live. Whoever does not keep the law will not live.

note.label: My Temple My Choice

precepts.why:
“Wherefore the law is holy, and the commandment holy”. When God says sanctify yourselves and be holy, you have to be applying the law, the statutes and the commandments. The churches do not want you to learn the Old Testament, because they do not want you to be saved. The scripture says choose life, but if you do not know what the law says, how are you going to choose life?

Solomon shows the way to life: “My son, keep my words, and lay up my commandments with thee. Keep my commandments, and live”. If you are not keeping the laws, you are not going to live. So when you keep eating unclean food and are not controlling what you eat, you are sinning.

“And my law as the apple of thine eye.” If somebody tried to poke your eye, you would move fast, like flash, because you do not take chances with something that could blind you. If somebody poked your arm you would not move that fast. The same way you protect your eye, you should protect the law. The moment anything tries to make you go against God’s law, you should move fast. But too many are like a fly drawn to the light that is about to kill it: instead of moving away, they keep going toward it.

The only way to have life is to keep the commandments as the apple of your eye, and that includes the command not to eat garbage and not to overeat. The Most High wants a fit army. You cannot step in the street teaching people discipline when you yourself do not have it.

precepts.text: What gives life is keeping the commandments.

precepts.point: The breath of life is twofold. One is the commandments, which were given to Adam; the other is the breathing life, the oxygen. Here everything on the dry land that breathed died; the fish were not touched.

note.label: Genesis 7: The First Rain and the Flood

precepts.why:
“Keep my commandments, and live; and my law as the apple of thine eye.” The commandments are the breath of life. That is the first side of the breath of life the Most High breathed into Adam: keep the commandments and live.

The people of Noah’s day despised the commandments, and so all in whose nostrils was the breath of life on the dry land died. Destruction came because of sin.

note.label: Genesis 38: Judah and Tamar

precepts.why:
“And, behold, there met him a woman with the attire of an harlot, and subtil of heart.” In the scriptures a harlot was always known by her dress. The attire spoke before she did.

That is why Judah, when he saw Tamar sitting in an open place by the way to Timnath, “thought her to be an harlot; because she had covered her face.” She had put off her widow’s garments, covered herself with a vail, and wrapped herself, and by that attire Judah took her for a harlot and turned in unto her, not knowing she was his daughter in law.

And she was subtil of heart too: she saw that Shelah was grown and she was not given unto him to wife, so she sat where Judah would pass, and took his signet, his bracelets and his staff as a pledge before she conceived by him.

precepts.point: He already told you what is up. The life he is telling you to choose is in Proverbs: keep my commandments and live. The commandments give you life; they are your spiritual force field out on the streets in the land of wickedness.

note.label: Deuteronomy 30: Call the Curses to Mind and Choose Life

precepts.why:
Highlight verse 19 if you do not have it highlighted: “I call heaven and earth to record this day against you, that I have set before you life and death, blessing and cursing: therefore choose life, that both thou and thy seed may live”. He already told you what is up: the blessing, the curse, and the way back. Now he says choose.

What is the life he tells you to choose? Solomon says it: “Keep my commandments, and live; and my law as the apple of thine eye.” The commandments give you life. They are your spiritual force field out on the streets in the land of wickedness. To choose life is to keep the commandments and hold the law as the apple of thine eye, and that is how both thou and thy seed may live.

note.label: Joshua 8: The Taking of Ai and the Blessings and Cursings

precepts.why: “Keep my commandments, and live; and my law as the apple of thine eye.” The life set before Israel in the blessings and cursings is the keeping of the commandments of the Most High; that is what life is. Death is the wages of sin. Joshua read every word of the law before all the congregation because that law is life to the one who keeps it, so choose life.

A lot of times we go out and think the scorner is somebody who does not want to hear, but it also goes into a youth who thinks he knows something but really does not.

note.label: Psalm 19: The Perfect Law That Converts the Soul

“For at the window of my house I looked through my casement, And beheld among the simple ones, I discerned among the youths, a young man void of understanding”. Solomon looked through his casement and saw among the simple ones a young man void of understanding.

Simple means you are void of understanding, the youth. The simple is not only somebody who does not want to hear; it also goes into a youth who thinks he knows something but really does not. That is who the testimony of the Lord makes wise.

note.label: Psalm 19: The Perfect Law That Converts the Soul

precepts.why:
“Keep my commandments, and live; and my law as the apple of thine eye.” Keep the commandments and live, and keep the law as the apple of your eye.

That is the commandment of the Lord enlightening the eyes. With the law as the apple of your eye, your eye is single and your whole body is full of light, and you know where to walk.

precepts.text: Women are to adorn themselves in modest apparel with shamefacedness and sobriety, the inward beauty and not the outward attire of the harlot.
precepts.point: So she caught him and kissed him, and with an impudent face said she had peace offerings and had paid her vows. This is the opposite of the modest apparel the sisters are taught.

note.label: Proverbs 7: The Adulteress Hunts for the Precious Soul

precepts.why:
“And, behold, there met him a woman with the attire of an harlot, and subtil of heart.” She does not go out with her head covered in a modest dress; she dresses in the clothing of a harlot, loud and stubborn, her feet not abiding in her house.

Paul gives the opposite, the way the sisters are taught: “In like manner also, that women adorn themselves in modest apparel, with shamefacedness and sobriety; not with broided hair, or gold, or pearls, or costly array”. Modest apparel with shamefacedness and sobriety is the inward beauty, and it is set against the outward attire of the harlot.

The woman in Proverbs 7 is everything 1 Timothy 2:9 tells the sisters not to be: the attire of an harlot on the outside, and subtil of heart and impudent of face on the inside.

precepts.text: Be ashamed of whoredom is the point set against the attire of the harlot.
precepts.point: So she caught him and kissed him, and with an impudent face said she had peace offerings and had paid her vows. This is the opposite of the modest apparel the sisters are taught.

note.label: Proverbs 7: The Adulteress Hunts for the Precious Soul

precepts.why:
“And, behold, there met him a woman with the attire of an harlot, and subtil of heart.” She is loud and stubborn, out in the streets, lying in wait at every corner, and “with an impudent face” she catches him and kisses him. There is no shame in her.

Ecclesiasticus says where the shame belongs: “Be ashamed of whoredom before father and mother: and of a lie before a prince and a mighty man”. Be ashamed of whoredom. That is the point set against the attire of the harlot: the modest woman is ashamed of whoredom before her father and mother, and the woman of Proverbs 7 wears it in the street with an impudent face.

precepts.text: The adulteress decks her bed with coverings and perfumes it with myrrh to entice her lover, the same way we prepared the bed of love for the Babylonians.
precepts.point: Yet she multiplied her whoredoms, calling to remembrance the days of her youth in Egypt, for she doted upon paramours whose flesh is as the flesh of asses and whose issue is like that of horses. Like a harlot who keeps seeking bigger because she has stopped feeling, we constantly sought the nations with the biggest and baddest idols.

note.label: Ezekiel 23: Aholah and Aholibah, the Two Harlot Sisters

precepts.why:
“And the Babylonians came to her into the bed of love”. The strange woman in Proverbs shows how that bed is prepared: “I have decked my bed with coverings of tapestry, with carved works, with fine linen of Egypt. I have perfumed my bed with myrrh, aloes, and cinnamon. Come, let us take our fill of love until the morning: let us solace ourselves with loves.”

That is the same way we prepared the bed of love for the Babylonians. And they “defiled her with their whoredom, and she was polluted with them, and her mind was alienated from them.” Just as a woman who lies with a man she is not married to becomes alienated and is left out there, so the Most High alienated His mind from us: “then my mind was alienated from her, like as my mind was alienated from her sister.”

Yet she multiplied her whoredoms, calling to remembrance the days of her youth in Egypt, doting upon paramours “whose flesh is as the flesh of asses, and whose issue is like the issue of horses.” Like a harlot who keeps seeking bigger because she has stopped feeling, we constantly sought the nations with the biggest and baddest idols.

note.label: Ezekiel 47: The Waters Issuing from the House

precepts.why:
The waters go toward the east country, down into the desert and into the sea, and the waters are healed: “every thing that liveth, which moveth, whithersoever the rivers shall come, shall live”. Life comes wherever the river comes.

The river is the word, and “Keep my commandments, and live; and my law as the apple of thine eye.” We receive life through the commandments. Life comes through keeping the law, so wherever the word of the Most High reaches and is kept, every thing shall live.
